title: Djokovic Loses to Hurkacz in Shanghai Days After Winning in Beijing
summary:
Tennis star Novak Djokovic had a big surprise at the Shanghai Masters in China. Just three days after winning the China Open in Beijing, he lost his second-round match to Hubert Hurkacz of Poland.

Hurkacz, who won the Shanghai tournament in 2023 and is ranked 34th in the world, won 6-4, 6-3 in 87 minutes. It was the first time he had ever beaten Djokovic. The two had played eight times before, and Djokovic had won every match.

Hurkacz is known for his powerful serve. Djokovic lost his serve just once in each set, and that was enough to decide the match.

"It's a special night," Hurkacz said. "I've been playing Novak for like seven years." He called Djokovic a legend and said it was a pleasure to share a court with him.

The loss came at the end of a busy stretch. It was Djokovic's sixth match in 10 days. In Beijing, the 39-year-old won the 102nd title of his career after his opponent in the final, Alex de Minaur, had to stop because of an injury. That title ended an 11-month wait for a trophy. It also meant Djokovic, who holds the men's record of 24 Grand Slam titles, has won at least one tour title for 21 years in a row.

Djokovic is trying to qualify for the ATP Finals, a special end-of-season event for the top eight players. He is currently ninth in the race, so he will need a strong result at the Paris Masters in November.

Also in Shanghai, Britain's Arthur Fery lost a long three-set match to Karen Khachanov that lasted about three and a half hours.
why_it_matters: Even the greatest champions can be beaten, and this loss makes Djokovic's push to reach the season-ending ATP Finals harder.
